newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian stock market to trade three times a week.
newsitem.headline: Latvian stock market to trade three times a week.

text.p: The Riga stock exchange said on Thursday that share trading will soon take place three times a week and hoped stock market sessions would take place daily by the end of this year or early next year.
Trading currently takes place on Tuesday and Thursday and a third trading session will be added on Wednesday from October 2, stock exchange chairman Uldis Cerps told Reuters.
"This a completely market-driven decision," Cerps said, noting that banks active on the exchange wanted a third session on Wednesday so they could trade three days in a row.
He said he hoped that trading four times a week would take place by the end of the year and daily soon after that.
"Activity is healthy, prices are going up and liquidity is increasing," Cerps added.
The stock exchange on Thursday turned over 40,750 lats, made up mostly of trade in market leader Unibanka on 21,840 lats.
The market, one of the newest in eastern Europe, opened in mid-1995 with a handful of shares.
It now regularly quotes 12 shares as well as government Treasury bills, although these are not often traded.
The market capitalisation is 61.39 million lats.
